findings.evidence: `RelativeCongr.lean:56-67` has the two elementwise membership lemmas and `:81-94` manually builds the equivalence; Mathlib’s generic fixer-conjugation API uses the stronger pattern at `mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/SubMulAction/OfFixingSubgroup.lean:225` (`fixingSubgroup_map_conj_eq`) and derives the equivalence at `:252` (`fixingSubgroupEquivFixingSubgroup`).
findings.fix: Add the subgroup-map equality first, prove the membership lemmas from it, and define `relativeDiffCongr` via subgroup transport rather than duplicating the inverse membership proof.
findings.issue: `diffCongr_mem_fixingSubgroup_image` proves only the forward elementwise special case, while the natural statement is the subgroup equality `(fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s).map (diffCongr e).toMonoidHom = fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) (e '' s)`; `diffCongr_symm_mem_fixingSubgroup` and the manual `relativeDiffCongr` are then derived special cases.

summary: The new API is below the natural Mathlib level for conjugating fixing subgroups: it exposes one-way membership and a hand-built subgroup equivalence instead of the subgroup-map equality from which both directions follow.
